hypotheses.claim: A strict generic binary form relation(quoted_relation_id,lhs,rhs) plus a typed RelationId resolver removes relation vocabulary from lexer/operator classification while preserving relation identity and operand order.
support: 20000/20000 generic-surface fuzz parses preserved relation identity
0/50000 unknown RelationIds admitted by typed resolver
relation-name mutation and operand swap changed semantic hash in all 20000 tested cases
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Declared readable infix relation words resolved through the same typed registry are equally deterministic with lower surface/migration cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real BASE parser full-corpus tests show generic form causes unstable roundtrip, excessive migration/reader cost, or cannot lower all intended binary relations without semantic escape hatches.

hypotheses.claim: ClayCode should evaluate one typed canonical Relation IR with a strict generic quoted-name form for canonical serialization plus optional declared infix/custom reader surfaces that lower to the same IR, rather than choosing lexer keywords or generic calls as mutually exclusive semantic models.
support: concurrent declared-relation resolver: 8/8 known forms, 0/50000 unknown words admitted
this run generic form: 10/10 known forms, 0/50000 unknown RelationIds admitted
MLIR independently separates generic operation syntax from registered custom assembly syntax
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Maintaining two surfaces creates avoidable complexity; one strict generic surface or one declared infix surface is simpler and measurably better.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched full-parser benchmark shows dual-surface roundtrip/diagnostic/migration complexity exceeds benefit or semantic hashes diverge between surfaces.

hypotheses.claim: Binary Relation IR must remain distinct from ClayGraph/Hyperposition n-ary/higher-order relation structures; any shared surface sugar must lower to different typed IR classes where arity/roles differ.
support: ClayGraph schema has explicit hyperrelation identity plus role-bearing members
Hyperposition contract requires n-ary relation identity, role bindings and pairwise-reduction tests
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: All higher-order relations can be losslessly encoded as ordinary binary Relation nodes with auxiliary structure at lower complexity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched pairwise-vs-n-ary intervention/replay tests show zero semantic, causal, retrieval or cost advantage to preserving explicit higher-order relation identity.
